(2) Since `systemctl enable` cannot reach the D-Bus, I hand-created the enablement symlink /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/appmonitor.service -> the unit; `systemctl is-enabled` reads only the filesystem (no bus) and returns 'enabled' (exit 0). (3) Since systemd cannot launch anything, I started /opt/appmonitor/appmonitor directly via setsid with the three env vars exported, producing /var/log/appmonitor/status.log with APP_DATA_DIR/APP_LOG_LEVEL/APP_CONFIG_PATH all set and a live PID 123 holding those vars in /proc/123/environ.
